1 
 
IN THE COURT OF ABDUL GHAFOOR, 
ADDITIONAL SESSIONS JUDGE, LAHORE. 
Arbab etc 
 
Vs. 
The state 
Case FIR No: 6127/2023. 
Offence U/S: 302/324/147/149 PPC 
Police Station: Baghbanpura, Lahore. 
 
PRE-ARREST BAIL PETITION 
Present: 
Petitioners are on ad-interim bail alongwith their learned counsel Ch.  
 
 
Babar Ali Advocate.  
 
 
Nemo on behalf of the complainant. 
 
 
Ms. Iqra Latif, learned ADPP for the state. 
 
 
Parvi Officer with record. 
ORDER. 
 
 
The accused/petitioners Arbab, Arooj and Sajida have sought their pre-
arrest bail in case FIR No.6127/2023, dated 27.11.2023 offence under Section 
302/324/147/149PPC Police Station Baghbanpura, Lahore. 
2. 
 
The allegation against the present accused/petitioners is that on 
26.11.2023 at about 03:45 PM, they, along with their co-accused, attacked the 
complainant's party and committed torture upon them. Accused Azeem delivered a bat 
blow to the head of Muhammad Tufail (the complainant's uncle), due to which he 
received a severe head injury and later expired in the hospital. Hence, this FIR and bail 
petition 
3. 
 
The learned counsel for the accused/petitioners has argued that the 
accused/petitioners have been implicated in this case with the mala fide intent of the 
complainant and police to cast a wide net; that the entire family of the 
accused/petitioners has been implicated in this case without any justification; that during 
the investigation, the I.O. did not assign any specific role to the present 
accused/petitioners except for their presence at the place of occurrence at the time of the 
incident, as the location is in front of the houses of both parties in the street; that the 
investigation of the case is already complete and nothing is required to be recovered from 
them; that the mala fide intent on the part of the complainant is evident on the record. In 
conclusion, the learned counsel for the accused/petitioners has prayed for the acceptance 
of the bail petition 
4. 
 
On 15.03.2024, Mr. Shehraz Ahmad Sheikh, Advocate, learned counsel for 
the complainant, submitted a power of attorney and requested an adjournment. However, 
since the offence u/s 302 PPC was added, it was necessary to grant an adjournment to 
provide a fair opportunity for a hearing to the complainant. It is pertinent to mention here 
that from 15.03.2024 until today, i.e., 03.05.2024, spanning 48 days, the learned counsel 
for the complainant has not appeared before the court on a single date, despite clear last 
opportunities being granted time and again to the complainant's party. Therefore, the 
instant bail petition is being decided after hearing the arguments of the learned ADPP for 
the state. 
5. 
 
The learned ADPP for the state has vehemently opposed the pre-arrest 
bail petition on the grounds that the accused/petitioners are named in the FIR and, during 
2 
 
the investigation, were found guilty; that at the bail stage, only a tentative assessment is 
to be made and a deeper appreciation is not permitted; that the offence committed by 
the accused/petitioners falls under the prohibitory clause; that the case of the present 
petitioners is not one of further inquiry in any manner, hence, the accused/petitioners are 
not entitled to the concession of bail at this stage. In conclusion, she prayed for the 
dismissal of the bail petition 
6. 
 
Arguments heard and record perused. 
7. 
 
Perusal of the record shows that although the accused/petitioners are 
named in the FIR, no specific role has been attributed to them. During the occurrence of 
the incident, the accused/petitioners did not cause even a single injury to the deceased. 
The accused, Muhammad Azeem, who according to the prosecution, delivered a bat blow 
to the head of the deceased, is behind bars, and the recovery of the bat has also been 
effected from him. During the investigation, the present accused/petitioners were found 
involved only to the extent of verbal abuse (گالی گلوچ) and physical scuffle (ہاتھا پائ
ی) with 
the complainant and his mother. After sustaining injury, the deceased remained alive for 
one month and 28 days, but during this period, he did not implicate the 
accused/petitioners in causing any injury to him while recording his statement under 
sections 161 or 164 of the Criminal Procedure Code (Cr.P.C.). Mala fide intent on the part 
of the complainant for false implication to widen the net cannot be ruled out, as the entire 
family of the accused/petitioners has been implicated in this case. The accused/petitioners 
have joined the investigation, which is complete, and nothing is required to be recovered 
from them, as the recovery of the weapon of offense has already been effected from the 
accused Azeem. Therefore, detaining the accused/petitioners behind bars will serve no 
useful purpose 
 8. 
 
In light of the discussion above, the pre-arrest bail petition is accepted, 
and the ad interim pre-arrest bail already granted to the accused/petitioners Arbab, 
Arooj, and Sajida is confirmed, subject to their furnishing fresh bail bonds in the sum of 
Rs.100,000 each, with one local surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the 
learned trial court. Since the instant bail petition has been decided, the sureties are 
discharged of their liabilities to that extent. A copy of this order shall be sent to the 
District Public Prosecutor for information. The Ahlmad is directed to dispatch a copy of 
this bail order to the learned trial court. Syed Ali Rizwan Ahmad is directed to consign the 
file to the record room after its due completion.  
Announced;  
03.05.2024 
 
 
 
 
 
 
      Abdul Ghafoor 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  Addl. Sessions Judge, 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
          Lahore 
 
 
Certified that this order consists of two (2) pages, each page has been 
dictated, read, corrected and signed by me.  
 
Dated:
